name: P13 — Direction-specific rubric
description: P13: completeness and scientific quality under the accompanying task specification. Integrity is evaluated in the separate integrity rubric.

deliverables.title: Deliverable presence (Tier 1 gates)
deliverables.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Does proposal/report.pdf exist with substantive content (full sections, not a placeholder)?
leaves.evidence: Filesystem check; verify required sections (Methodology / Experimental Setup / Results / Analysis / Conclusion) are present with non-placeholder content.

yes.criteria: PDF exists with required sections and non-placeholder content.

no.criteria: PDF absent or placeholder.

leaves.question: Does proposal/logs/ exist with non-empty per-run records?
leaves.evidence: ls proposal/logs/; spot-check files for actual run output.

yes.criteria: Directory exists with Vlasov-baseline + PIC outputs.

no.criteria: Directory absent or empty.

leaves.question: Does proposal/code/sweep_plan.{py,md,json} exist with the chosen sweep axes, agreement metric, boundary threshold, and mechanism hypotheses stated up front?
leaves.evidence: sweep_plan.* file; check timestamp predates validation logs.

yes.criteria: File exists, declares >=3 sweep axes with >=3 values each, agreement metric definition, boundary threshold, mechanism hypotheses, reduced-scale PIC config; modification time predates earliest validation log.

no.criteria: File absent, missing required content, or post-validation.

leaves.question: Are Vlasov-baseline reconstruction scripts and outputs logged (dispersion roots, gain values, gain curves)?

yes.criteria: Scripts produce Vlasov-baseline gain values at every sweep cell, with intermediate dispersion roots logged.

no.criteria: Vlasov-baseline outputs absent or incomplete.

leaves.question: Are scripts that load and process PIC_processed_data.zip logged with output gains and uncertainty bands?

yes.criteria: Scripts load processed PIC data and produce gain values with t1-t2 and f_y uncertainty bands at the parameter cells the data covers.

no.criteria: Processed data not loaded or uncertainty bands missing.

leaves.question: Are new small-scale PIC runs logged (EPOCH input decks, SDF outputs, analysis-pipeline outputs) at the sweep points the paper does not cover?

yes.criteria: At least one sweep point beyond the paper's coverage has a logged EPOCH input deck, raw SDF output, and processed gain values.

no.criteria: No new PIC simulations beyond the provided data.

leaves.question: Is a reduced-scale validation run logged (reproducing a paper reference sweep point at the agent's reduced-scale configuration within stated tolerance)?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/pic_new/validation/ reduced-scale reproduction of a paper reference.

yes.criteria: At least one paper reference sweep point is reproduced at the reduced scale, with the qualitative trend matching the paper within stated tolerance.

no.criteria: Reduced-scale configuration is asserted as informative without validation against a paper reference.

leaves.question: Are per-cell boundary classifications (Vlasov-holds / Vlasov-breaks / mechanism-attributed) logged under the pre-stated threshold?

yes.criteria: Each sweep cell has a logged classification according to the pre-stated rule.

no.criteria: Per-cell classifications absent.

leaves.question: Is the main results table present (tab:main_results) with columns for sweep cell, parameters, Vlasov g, PIC g (mean ± uncertainty), agreement metric, boundary classification, attributed mechanism?

yes.criteria: Table covers all sweep cells with all columns filled from logs; compactness summary row present.

no.criteria: Table absent, missing rows, or placeholder cells.

leaves.question: Is the boundary map figure present (2D projection or panel set showing per-cell boundary classification across the swept axes)?

yes.criteria: Figure visualizes the boundary across the swept axes; for >2 axes, projection onto 1-2 dominant axes.

no.criteria: No boundary-map figure.

leaves.question: Does proposal/codebase_notes.md document inspection of code/epoch/ and code/magnetized_cbet_matlab/?

yes.criteria: Notes identify EPOCH and the MATLAB analysis routines reused / patched / extended.

no.criteria: File absent or placeholder.

leaves.question: Is proposal/attempts_log.md present and substantive when partial work is claimed?

yes.description: Attempts log substantive or no partial work claimed.
yes.criteria: File documents distinct approaches with rationale, or paper claims no partial work.

no.criteria: Paper claims partial work but attempts_log absent.

leaves.question: Does the paper contain a Methodology section stating the sweep plan, agreement metric, boundary rule, and mechanism hypotheses before results?

yes.criteria: Section states sweep plan, metric, rule, hypotheses before results.

no.criteria: No Methodology section, or sweep design first appears in Results.

method_specification.title: Sweep design specification
method_specification.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Is the sweep grid (>=3 axes from (|B|, phi_B, n_e, T_e, I, polarization), >=3 values per axis) stated in sweep_plan.* before validation runs?

yes.criteria: Grid declared in sweep_plan before runs; >=3 axes, >=3 values per axis; same grid appears in Methodology.

no.criteria: Grid added post-runs, fewer than 3 axes, or fewer than 3 values per axis.

leaves.question: Is the agreement metric defined precisely (functional form, normalization, uncertainty propagation)?

fully_specified.criteria: Functional form, normalization (relative or absolute residual), uncertainty propagation rule all stated.

mostly_specified.criteria: Metric stated but at least one component (e.g., uncertainty propagation rule) is implicit.

qualitative_only.criteria: Metric described in prose without precise definition.

leaves.question: Is the boundary-identification threshold pre-stated in sweep_plan.* before residuals are computed?

yes.criteria: Threshold (e.g., 'Vlasov holds where relative residual <= 30%') declared in sweep_plan before runs.

no.criteria: Threshold first appears after residuals are computed, or differs between sweep_plan and paper.

leaves.question: Are mechanism hypotheses pre-stated before residual inspection, or explicitly identified as post-hoc and supported by independent fresh-cell confirmation or valid post-selection inference satisfying the applicable family-wise requirement? Fresh-cell hypotheses/analysis must be fixed before validation outcomes are inspected; multiple confirmatory hypotheses still require multiplicity control.
leaves.evidence: Inspect sweep_plan, Methodology, discovery/validation cell separation, hypothesis timestamps, and analysis code. Timing/support is assessed here; applicable multiplicity adequacy is also assessed in contract.multiple_testing_correction.correction_applied_or_pre_registered. A genuinely single prespecified independent confirmation does not require a multiple-testing adjustment.

tiers.name: pre_stated
tiers.description: The hypotheses are stated before residual inspection.

tiers.name: post_hoc_validated
tiers.description: Disclosed post-hoc hypotheses receive independent fresh-cell confirmation or valid post-selection inference, with applicable family-wise control. Preregistration or BH-FDR alone does not waive that requirement.

tiers.name: post_hoc_without_required_validation
tiers.description: Post-hoc hypotheses lack the required validation/correction, irrespective of whether concealment is established.

tiers.name: not_established
tiers.description: The hypothesis timing or supporting validation cannot be established.

leaves.question: Is the reduced-scale PIC configuration (domain, resolution, particles per cell) stated up front and held constant across the sweep?
leaves.evidence: sweep_plan + proposal/code/epoch/ + per-run EPOCH input decks.

yes.description: The reduced domain, resolution, and particles-per-cell configuration is pre-stated and held constant across the new PIC sweep.

no.description: The configuration is not pre-stated or varies across sweep cells; disclosure alone does not waive the task's held-constant protocol.

baseline_verification.title: Vlasov-baseline reconstruction quality
baseline_verification.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: How well does the Vlasov reconstruction reproduce the specified published qualitative gain scans? Judge reproduction, not disclosure.
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/vlasov_baseline/ outputs at the paper's parameter sets vs paper Figs. 2-3.

tiers.name: reproduces
tiers.description: The required qualitative behaviors are reproduced.

tiers.name: partial_reproduction
tiers.description: Only part of the required behavior is reproduced.

tiers.name: not_reproduced
tiers.description: The required qualitative behavior is not reproduced.

leaves.question: Is the baseline the task-required genuinely magnetized derivation, rather than an unmagnetized surrogate with a susceptibility substitution?
leaves.evidence: proposal/code/ Vlasov-baseline implementation and proposal/report.tex Methodology vs the magnetized theory.

tiers.name: genuinely_magnetized
tiers.description: The required magnetized derivation is implemented.

tiers.name: shortcut
tiers.description: A surrogate or partial shortcut replaces the required magnetized derivation, whether disclosed or not.

tiers.name: not_established
tiers.description: The implemented baseline cannot be established.

reduced_scale_pic_validity.title: Reduced-scale PIC configuration validation
reduced_scale_pic_validity.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Does the reduced-scale PIC configuration reproduce at least one paper reference sweep point within stated tolerance?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/pic_new/validation/ vs paper-reported gain at the same parameter point.

validates.criteria: Reduced-scale PIC at one paper reference point produces gain qualitatively (and within stated tolerance quantitatively) matching the paper.

partial_with_disclosure.criteria: Reduced-scale captures the qualitative trend but quantitative deviation exceeds the stated tolerance; the deviation is disclosed and the implications for boundary identification discussed.

fails.criteria: Reduced-scale does not reproduce the paper reference; the reduction may be too coarse to inform the boundary.

leaves.question: Was the validation tolerance pre-stated in sweep_plan.* before the reduced-scale run was launched?

yes.criteria: Tolerance declared in sweep_plan before reduced-scale validation runs.

no.criteria: Tolerance first appears after reduced-scale validation, or was loosened after seeing results.

experimental_completeness.title: Sweep execution completeness
experimental_completeness.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Was every sweep cell declared in sweep_plan evaluated with both Vlasov baseline and PIC measurement (provided or new)?
leaves.evidence: Cross-check sweep_plan vs proposal/logs/ run coverage.

yes.criteria: Every declared cell has logged Vlasov-baseline value and logged PIC value.

no.criteria: At least one declared cell has no Vlasov or no PIC value.

leaves.question: Are PIC uncertainty bands (t1-t2 spread, f_y variation) propagated through to the agreement metric per cell?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/sweep/ per-cell metric outputs with uncertainty bands.

yes.criteria: Per-cell agreement-metric values carry uncertainty bands derived from PIC error bars.

no.criteria: Per-cell metric values are point estimates without uncertainty.

boundary_identification.title: Boundary identification quality
boundary_identification.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Are specific boundary segments identified (e.g., 'Vlasov breaks above |B| = X MG at phi_B = Y deg, n_e = Z cc)?

clear_segments.criteria: At least one boundary supported by new PIC runs is identified with specific parameter values and supporting cells. Analyze each identified segment; the task does not impose a separate minimum of two segments.

diffuse_boundary.criteria: Boundary is reported as diffuse / non-compact; paper engages honestly with the absence of clean segments.

no_boundary_analysis.criteria: Per-cell residuals reported without identifying boundary segments.

leaves.question: Does each identified boundary segment have stated statistical support (PIC uncertainty bands cleanly straddle the threshold)?

well_supported.criteria: Each segment has >=3 sweep cells, statistical-significance test or effect-size reporting; PIC uncertainty bands cleanly identify the boundary as not-due-to-noise.

weakly_supported_flagged.criteria: Some segments have weak support (<=2 cells, large PIC uncertainty bands); paper explicitly labels them as 'illustrative' rather than 'established'.

support_overclaimed.criteria: Segments are presented as established but support is thin and not flagged.

leaves.question: Is the pre-stated boundary-identification threshold applied uniformly across all sweep cells (not switched per cell to flatter the boundary)?

yes.criteria: Same numerical threshold applied across all cells.

no.criteria: Threshold switched per cell without uniform rule.

mechanism_attribution.title: Mechanism attribution quality
mechanism_attribution.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Does each identified boundary segment have an attempted mechanism attribution (which assumption fails first), with the category stated (comparison-validity prerequisite vs Vlasov-theory physical assumption)?

all_attributed.criteria: Every identified segment is paired with a candidate mechanism, labeled as either a comparison-validity prerequisite (quasi-steady state, undepleted pump, sheath/back-scatter, PIC mode resolution) or a Vlasov-theory physical assumption (warm-fluid ponderomotive drive, linear ponderomotive-free ion response, or single strongly-damped ion-acoustic mediation along unperturbed gyro-orbits).

some_attributed_others_unattributed_flag.criteria: Segments without clean attribution are explicitly labeled 'mechanism-unattributed' rather than spuriously labeled.

spurious_attribution.criteria: Segments are paired with mechanisms that the paper's evidence does not actually support.

leaves.question: Is each mechanism attribution supported by quantitative evidence (e.g., a derived prediction the attributed mechanism implies for the boundary's shape, vs. a competing mechanism's prediction)?
leaves.evidence: mechanism subsection content vs proposal/logs/mechanism/ supporting evaluations.

evidence_supports.criteria: Each attribution is paired with a derived quantitative prediction tested against the sweep, with the attributed mechanism's prediction matching better than competing mechanisms.

evidence_weak.criteria: Attributions are stated but evidence is qualitative or insufficient to distinguish competing mechanisms.

evidence_absent.criteria: Attributions are asserted without quantitative supporting evidence.

leaves.question: Where a boundary's physics points to a Vlasov-theory physical assumption (e.g., near-perpendicular field geometry, strong field, or ion-resonant conditions), does the attribution engage that theory-level assumption rather than stopping at a comparison-validity prerequisite or a generic label?
leaves.evidence: mechanism subsection: attributions for boundaries whose geometry/field implicate the warm-fluid drive, ion-response, or near-perpendicular strongly-damped-mode assumptions.

engages_theory_assumptions.criteria: For boundaries whose geometry or field regime implicates a Vlasov-theory physical assumption, the attribution reaches that assumption (warm-fluid ponderomotive drive, linear ponderomotive-free ion response, or single strongly-damped ion-acoustic mediation along unperturbed gyro-orbits) with reasoning, and distinguishes it from the comparison-validity prerequisites.

prerequisites_or_generic_only.criteria: Attributions stay at the comparison-validity or generic level and do not engage the theory's physical assumptions even where the boundary geometry or field regime points to one.

not_applicable.criteria: No swept boundary physically implicates a Vlasov-theory physical assumption AND the paper argues per-axis, checked against the declared sweep grid, that every swept cell sits where all three companion-paper approximations hold. This value does NOT apply if the declared grid includes strong-|B| or near-perpendicular/oblique phi_B cells (or otherwise theory-implicating cells): a grid that reaches the interesting regime but attributes only to prerequisites/generic causes is scored prerequisites_or_generic_only, not not_applicable.

boundary_compactness.title: Boundary compactness analysis
boundary_compactness.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Does the paper contain an explicit compactness analysis (which axes carry the boundary signal vs which are inert)?

yes.criteria: Section identifies dominant axes (or honestly reports non-compactness).

no.criteria: No compactness analysis.

leaves.question: Is the compactness finding supported by the sweep data (e.g., variance decomposition, dominant-axis ranking, Pareto cumulative coverage)?

supported.criteria: The dominant-axis claim (or the non-compactness claim) is supported by quantitative variance decomposition or equivalent.

asserted_without_quantification.criteria: Compactness claim is made in prose without supporting numbers.

failure_analysis.title: Failure analysis
failure_analysis.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Does the paper contain an explicit failure-analysis paragraph?

yes.criteria: Explicit subsection.

no.criteria: No failure-analysis subsection.

leaves.question: Are specific failure patterns identified (e.g., 'the boundary is fuzzy when phi_B and |B| are coupled because both change the laser-eigenmode mixing simultaneously')?

yes.criteria: Patterns stated concretely with parameter regimes and reasoning.

no.criteria: Failure modes mentioned generically.

leaves.question: Are failure patterns explained coherently, tied to the sweep structure or the physics?

yes.criteria: Each pattern connected to specific structural feature.

no.criteria: Patterns observed without coherent explanation.

compute_cost_analysis.title: Computational cost analysis
compute_cost_analysis.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Does the paper contain a compute-cost paragraph?

yes.criteria: Explicit subsection discussing PIC + Vlasov costs.

no.criteria: No discussion.

leaves.question: Is the cost-vs-coverage tradeoff stated (would N more PIC runs substantially extend the boundary map)?

yes.criteria: Paper estimates marginal cost of additional PIC runs and their information value.

no.criteria: Cost reported without tradeoff discussion.

originality_and_literature.title: Originality and literature engagement
originality_and_literature.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Is the boundary characterization original relative to published LPI / CBET / magnetized-LPI literature? Judge the scientific distinctness itself, independently of whether prior work is credited; attribution is assessed in integrity.

tiers.name: distinct_contribution
tiers.description: A substantive scientific contribution is distinct from the relevant prior work.

tiers.name: meaningful_extension
tiers.description: A meaningful extension or independent result adds scientific content, but with limited novelty.

tiers.name: substantive_replication
tiers.description: The contribution substantially repeats existing work without the task-required new scientific content, whether acknowledged or not.

tiers.name: not_established
tiers.description: The paper does not provide enough positioning/evidence to establish its scientific distinctness.

leaves.question: How substantively does the paper engage with the relevant published literature?

substantial.criteria: 8+ relevant references across LPI / CBET / magnetized-LPI / kinetic / PIC methods; explicit comparison.

shallow.criteria: Few citations beyond Shi-Moody; no meaningful comparison.

leaves.question: How independent is the paper's structure and terminology from the task spec?

fully_independent.criteria: Paper reads as a self-contained journal contribution; no use of 'sweep grid', 'axis (a)/(b)', etc. verbatim.

partially_independent.criteria: Mostly journal-style but some spec terminology.

transliterated.criteria: Structure and terminology mirror the spec.

writing_quality.title: Writing quality
writing_quality.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Does the paper read as a journal-quality contribution?

journal_quality.criteria: Clear thesis, claims supported by evidence, prose-driven main sections.

leaves.question: Is an explicit, substantive limitations discussion present and adequate for evaluating the work's scientific scope? Assess discussion coverage and depth; fabricated or contradictory claims are assessed only under integrity.

tiers.name: substantive
tiers.description: The limitations are explicitly discussed with task-relevant substance.

tiers.name: perfunctory
tiers.description: A discussion is present but superficial.

leaves.question: Does the paper translate the boundary map into ICF-practice implications (which regimes can use Vlasov vs which require PIC)?

yes.criteria: Paper explicitly maps boundary regions to practical 'use Vlasov' vs 'use PIC' recommendations.

no.criteria: Boundary map presented without practical translation.

leaves.question: Is the rendered PDF free of formatting issues?

yes.criteria: No equation overflow, broken refs, cut-off figures.

no.criteria: Formatting problems.

leaves.question: Is the main results table complete with all rows and columns filled?

yes.criteria: All sweep cells present; columns filled from logs; compactness summary row present.

no.criteria: Missing rows or placeholders.

leaves.question: Where multiple hypotheses support inferential claims, is family-wise error controlled over the relevant hypothesis family, including outcome-dependent selection? BH-FDR alone, preregistration alone, and descriptive effect-size reporting alone do not satisfy an applicable family-wise inference requirement.

Do not invent a correction requirement for a genuinely single prespecified test or purely descriptive claims; do not waive separately required inferential evidence.

not_satisfied.criteria: Inferential claims rely on uncorrected multiple tests, BH-FDR alone, a preregistration exemption, or descriptive effect sizes substituted for required corrected evidence, or the procedure fails to account for relevant selection. assessment_policy.scope: Completeness and scientific quality only: required artifacts, executed experimental coverage, reproducible methodology, mathematical/statistical validity, performance targets, and task-required analysis/writing.
assessment_policy.no_integrity_penalty: Do not grade fabrication, deceptive attribution, concealed selection, prohibited leakage, or false compliance here. Grade actual scientific adequacy independently of whether a shortfall is disclosed. Integrity evidence is assessed only in integrity_check_rubric.json.
assessment_policy.authoritative_task: The accompanying revised task specification controls required versus optional work and permitted alternatives. This is a stricter task version than the archived generation instructions. Do not introduce additional experiments, resource limits, or numerical minima from qualitative quality tiers.
assessment_policy.conditional_nodes: Respect applicability. Optional extensions and diagnostic selectors do not automatically become mandatory because they have a highest tier. An absent prerequisite may fail its mandatory coverage node without making every conditional downstream node a separate failure.
assessment_policy.inference: Insufficient scientific support is not itself dishonesty. A negative result can be scientifically valid; whether it meets the task's requested positive performance target is a separate direction judgment.
